Zig `std` has no load balancer.

**Where we are ahead:** the only reusable Zig upstream-pool library found; passive (breaker)
and active (`healthTick`) health kept orthogonal, bulkhead per upstream, pick-as-full-admission
with a `PickGuard`, deterministic virtual-clock tests, no ambient clock or entropy.
**Where we are behind:** no locality-aware balancing, no service discovery (→ *What is deliberately not done*; DNS
resolution belongs to `dns`). Runtime add/remove/drain with safe
retirement, consistent hashing on a ring (`ring_hash`, `pickByKey`) and power-of-two-choices
(`least_request`) exist.

Design + threat notes for auditors. Usage: see ./README.md. Attribution/provenance: see ./README.md (no NOTICE entry — own code, design references only).

## Design & invariants
Pick is a full admission: a non-null `pick()` has already taken the upstream's bulkhead slot and
breaker admission and bumped in-flight — every successful pick must be followed by exactly one
`report()` (`call()` does this automatically); a lost report leaks the slot and, under a half-open
breaker, the probe budget. Passive vs. active health are orthogonal: `report(u, ok, rtt_ns)` feeds
the breaker only (`failure_threshold` consecutive failures trip it, `pick` skips until cooldown
admits a probe); `healthTick(now_ns)` is caller-driven and separate — a failing check sets a down mark
(skipped regardless of breaker state), a passing check clears the mark and doubles as the breaker's
recovery probe, walking `open → half_open → closed` across ticks without risking a live request.
Eight strategies (`Strategy` enum; the last two are described under "Ring hash" and "Time-driven weights, ejection, priorities" below): `round_robin` (default, strict rotation), `random` (uniform,
seeded `std.Random` from `Options.seed` — no ambient entropy), `weighted_round_robin` (smooth WRR,
the nginx algorithm — each healthy upstream chosen exactly `weight` times per window of
`sum(weights)`, interleaved not bursty), `least_connections` (fewest in-flight), `ewma_latency`
(lowest EWMA of reported RTTs; never-measured upstreams score 0 and are tried first for warm-up), `least_request`, `ring_hash`, `maglev`. No
hidden clock: `healthTick` is caller-driven; the breaker's clock is injected via
`Options.breaker.clock`; the RTT stopwatch inside `call()` uses `Options.clock`. Concurrency:
`pick`/`report`/`call`/`healthTick`/stats are internally synchronized (a pool spinlock for strategy
state plus atomic counters); the breaker/bulkhead synchronize themselves independently; membership (`add`/`remove`/`drain`/`reap`, see below) may change while the pool serves and only `deinit` is single-owner teardown; the
injected `HealthChecker` runs outside the pool lock since it may perform I/O. Bounded, typed-error,
no panics: the fleet is capped by `max_upstreams`; a malformed `host:port` is a typed error; `call()`
returns the first success, the last operation error once `max_tries` picks are exhausted, or
`error.NoHealthyUpstream` when nothing was pickable. Composes two siblings rather than reimplementing
them: a per-upstream `resilience.CircuitBreaker` (passive health) and optional per-upstream
`resilience.Bulkhead` (concurrency cap), plus `probe`'s `Connector` seam for active checks.
Clean-room; design references Envoy/HAProxy upstream-cluster semantics and resilience4j's Bulkhead
(behavior only) — see README Provenance.

**Time-driven weights, ejection, priorities.** `pick` reads no clock: slow start and outlier ejection move with
`Pool.tick(now_ns)`, called from the caller's loop like `healthTick`.
- *Slow start* (`Options.slow_start`, Envoy `slow_start_config`): `.weighted_round_robin` weighs a member by
  `weight × max(min_weight_percent, (age / window)^(1 / aggression))` (Envoy's formula, defaults 10 % and 1.0), in
  thousandths so the smooth-WRR arithmetic stays integer. A member starts at the minimum on `add` and its age begins
  at the next tick; one that `healthTick` brings back from down starts over. Other strategies do not consult weights.
- *Outlier ejection* (`Options.outlier`, Envoy's `success_rate` detector): each `interval_ns` the members with at least
  `request_volume` reports in the window are compared; one below `mean - stdev_factor × stdev` (population) is ejected
  for `base_ejection_ns × times ejected`; at most `max_ejection_percent` of the members (at least one) are out at a
  time, nothing happens below `minimum_hosts` qualifying members, and a member that passes a window clean earns back
  one ejection. `pick` skips an ejected member (`admit`); `UpstreamStats.ejected`, `healthy`. Consecutive failures stay
  the breaker's, so the two are orthogonal.
- *Priorities* (`UpstreamSpec.priority`; nginx `backup`, Envoy priority levels): every strategy first picks among the
  lowest level and moves up only when no member of it is admissible. Strict failover; Envoy's overprovisioning
  spill-over is not modelled.
- *Maglev* (`Strategy.maglev`): Eisenbud et al. (NSDI 2016) §3.4 with Envoy's weighted turns; table size
  `maglev_table_size` (a prime, default 65537), slots claimed along each member's `(offset + j × skip) mod M`
  permutation from two `XxHash64` seeds of its id. Tests pin the balance (shares differ by one slot), weights 1:2:3
  within a few percent, that a removal moves few keys of the survivors, and the walk past a down owner; there is no
  external oracle for the exact table.

**Membership while serving.** `add`, `remove`, `drain`/`undrain`, `reap`, `getById`,
`count` and `stats` take the pool lock (`add`/`remove` allocate under it). `remove(id)` sets
`draining` and `retired`, `orderedRemove`s the member (registration order, so least-conn/EWMA
ties stay stable), moves it to `retired`, keeps the rotation on the member that followed it, and
rebuilds the ring. A retired member stays allocated while `in_flight > 0` or `pins > 0`; `reap`
frees the others. `report` releases its hold LAST (the in-flight decrement), so nothing touches a
member after that point. `healthTick` dups the member list under the lock, pins each, checks outside
the lock, unpins under it; `health_busy` makes a tick that starts during another a no-op (incl. one
started from inside a check). `undrain` never revives a retired member.

**Ring hash.** Points `XxHash64(seed 0, id ++ "-" ++ decimal(j))` for `j < k`, `k = weight ×
ring_points_per_weight`, or each member's proportional share of `max_ring_points` when the ring
would exceed it (never below 1) — so the ring is at most `max_ring_points + members` points.
Sorted by (hash, member index); a key's owner is the first point with hash ≥ `XxHash64(key)`
(lower bound, wrapping). A pick walks one lap at most, trying each distinct member once
(`ring_refused` marks, reset after the walk), so a refused owner's keys go to the next member on
the ring and nobody else's move. Ids, not addresses, are hashed: a member keeps its keys across
an address change. **P2C:** two distinct indices from the seeded PRNG (the second drawn from the
other `len-1`), fewer in-flight wins, ties to the first draw; weights not consulted.

## Threat model / out of scope
Not a security primitive: does not authenticate upstreams, does not encrypt/verify traffic, and
trusts whatever health signal (`HealthChecker`, `report(ok=...)`) the caller feeds it — a caller
reporting false health defeats both passive and active health without any detection here. Retried
attempts inside `call()`'s failover may repeat side effects; only idempotent operations are safe to
route this way (same caveat `resilience` documents for its own retry). No congestion control or
backpressure signaling to callers beyond the per-upstream bulkhead cap and `NoHealthyUpstream`/
`BulkheadFull` errors. Active health I/O correctness (e.g. TCP connect semantics) is `probe`'s
responsibility, not this module's.

## Verification

- **Run:** `scripts/modtest upstream` (`zig build test-upstream`).
- **Tests:** fully offline and deterministic (scripted fake operation + fake `HealthChecker` + virtual clock, no
  sockets): registration bounds, duplicates and parse errors; every strategy (rotation, exact smooth-WRR split,
  least-connections, EWMA warm-up, seeded random reproducible, P2C never picks a member that loses every pair);
  breaker trip, skip and re-admission after the cooldown; bulkhead-full skipping; `call()` failover (`max_tries`,
  last error, `NoHealthyUpstream`); `healthTick` marking down/up, interval gating, and the breaker walking
  `open → half_open → closed`; per-upstream and pool stats.
- **Ring oracle:** ring owners are held to Python's `xxhash` package driven as a black box in a one-off run (the expected values
  are frozen in the test, which builds the same ring by the documented rule; no tool is kept in the module), plus the key distribution over
  weights 1:2:3. Invariants: removal moves only the removed member's keys, an added member takes keys only for
  itself, a down owner's keys walk on while everyone else's stay, a key spelled like a point lands on that
  point's member, the ring bound.
- **Membership:** report after remove, reap only idle members, re-add of a removed id, the rotation after removing
  the member it pointed at, drain under every strategy, a member removed and reaped from inside a health check
  (pinned), a nested tick; a seeded model sweep (every strategy; add/remove/drain/undrain/pick/pickByKey/report/
  healthTick/reap against a model: no inadmissible pick, null only when no member is admissible, in-flight equals
  the model's holds, `reap` frees exactly the idle retired members, no stale ring index, no leak, reach pinned).
- **Concurrency:** a 4-thread `call()` hammer asserts the per-upstream bulkhead cap is never exceeded and no slot
  leaks; a `call()` + churn-thread test (remove/reap/re-add).
- **Fuzz / constant time:** no fuzz obligation under check-fuzz; ct n/a.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation
  run and the delta runs after it.
- **Mutation run (2026-11-25, whole module):** 219 mutants (Maglev, priorities, slow start, success-rate outlier ejection, the rest of the pool): 204 killed (6 by hang), 15 equivalent. The Maglev table is pinned against an independent re-implementation of the weighted fill. The `Pool.report` saturation guard (fixed 2026-11-26) is killed in a ReleaseFast build by the release-only test; in ReleaseSafe its mutants are masked by the panic that fires first, by design.

## What is deliberately not done

- **Service discovery / DNS resolution** — belongs to `dns`; the pool takes `host:port` members.
- **Locality / zone-aware balancing** (Envoy): nginx, HAProxy, traefik and tower have none; it needs per-member
  locality metadata and panic thresholds. Failover between levels is `UpstreamSpec.priority`.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.
